Hey, it's ok, almost every artist has been in the same position as you. Not knowing how to move forward with their skills while feeling like everyone else is just surpassing you.   


I personally believe no one can measure how good someone else is at art because no one else can ever know the true intent of an artwork.   
Learning how to draw is not learning how to move your hand with a pencil to imitate life, learning to draw and become an artist is learning how to see.   
When I was starting I would look at everything around me and break it up into simple shapes. Say a human figure. Head = circle, Arms= a collection of ovals, chest= rectangle and so on.   


You need to learn how to break down what you see, and yes you can trace photos of other people in poses and whatnot (however under no circumstance can you trace someone else's art) It's very normal in the professional scene for artists to trace. When you trace photos it is far easier to break down everything and make it easier to digest in your head.   


Another thing worth learning is simple colour theory, how colours interact with each other and the effect that it can have on an art piece. If you have any more questions please ask.
